title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'ateliers'. These are lattices F of 'tame' subsets with two relations, ≤ and ≪, and an underlying set M of multistrata. The page continues p.47's definition of a 'quasi-plongement' (quasi-embedding) f: F' → F. Such an f is monotone for ≤ and ≪, and commutes with Sup (so it sends ∅ to ∅) and with Inf.

Step 1. He states a desired extra axiom, (1.54). For F'' = f(F'), the map Ssf_{i0}(F') → Ssf_{i0}(F''), G' ↦ f(G'), should be bijective. Ssf is presumably the set of closed 'sub-stratified' parts of a given type i0. The margin note says that, by (1.54), it would suffice that f(F') be a (closed?) part of F.

Step 2. Without assuming f injective, he expects, 'in all cases known to me', a canonical surjective monotone map (1.55), φ = φ_{f,F'}: F̃ → F̃'. Here F̃ is the poset canonically attached to an atelier: its poset of strata or 'points', whose closed (down-)sets Pf(F̃) model the closed tame parts.

Step 3. (1.54) should then be recovered as inverse image (1.56): Pf(F̃') → Pf(F̃), A ↦ φ^{-1}(A). In addition, the preorder on F̃ should be the inverse image of the order on F̃'.

Step 4. Cases:
- If f is injective and (1.54) holds, φ is an isomorphism of ordered sets.
- In general he requires (1.54) to be (at least) surjective.
- In the important cases, e.g. 𝓕 → Fig(𝓛), (1.54) is bijective even when f is not injective.

Step 5. When (1.54) comes from some monotone φ, that φ is unique. This is proved on p.49. Monotone maps I → I' embed injectively into maps Pf(I') → Pf(I) commuting with arbitrary unions and finite intersections, i.e. into topos morphisms Top(I) → Top(I'). These are continuous maps from I to the sobrification of I'.

In modern terms: a stratification is a continuous map to a poset with its Alexandrov topology. A morphism of tame structures should induce a map of strata posets, with closed unions of strata pulled back as down-sets. The 'inverse-image order' condition is exactly what makes φ^{-1} bijective on closed sets. The purpose is functoriality of the strata-poset construction for (quasi-)embeddings of ateliers.
errors: There is a mild tension in the statement. If φ is surjective and the order on F̃ is the inverse image of that on F̃', then φ^{-1} on closed sets is automatically bijective, not merely surjective. Grothendieck himself notes on p.49 that 'inverse-image topology' is equivalent to surjectivity of (1.54), so the conditions overlap or are redundant.

The direction of (1.55), F̃ → F̃' with F̃ attached to f(F') or F, is not made fully explicit. Notation switches between F, F'' = f(F') and F. This is a gap in the notes rather than a mathematical error.
The conditions are heuristic ('dans tous les cas à ma connaissance'); no proof is given that φ exists.

ideas.what: Quasi-embeddings of 'ateliers' (axiomatic tame-topology structures) required to induce bijections on closed stratified sub-objects
ideas.modern_name: morphisms of stratified spaces / o-minimal structure embeddings; functoriality of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's tame topology programme; later o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches tame topology, but not 'ateliers' or this axiom

ideas.what: A canonical monotone (surjective) map of strata posets φ: F̃ → F̃' with closed parts pulled back by φ^{-1} and the order on F̃ being the inverse image
ideas.modern_name: stratification as a continuous map to a poset with the Alexandrov topology; pullback of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A) and the exit-path literature (MacPherson, Treumann)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the poset map inducing a given map on closed sets (p.49 lemma: monotone maps ↔ union-preserving, finite-intersection-preserving maps of down-set lattices ↔ topos morphisms)
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov/Stone duality for preorders; points of the presheaf topos; sobrification
ideas.where_published: SGA4 IV treats points/sober spaces in general

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes, as part of the definition of morphisms of ateliers, that every quasi-embedding induces a canonical surjective map of strata posets realizing the map on closed stratified sub-objects by inverse image. He observes that in key examples (𝓕 → Fig(𝓛)) this is bijective even for non-injective f. The axiom is left heuristic and unproved.
missed.quote: Sans supposer f injective, dans tous les cas à ma connaissance, on aura une application canonique (surjective) F̃ → F̃' ... de telle façon que (1.54) en soit déduite par l'application en sens inverse A ↦ φ^{-1}(A)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the now-standard view of stratifications as maps to Alexandrov posets, functorial under pullback. This viewpoint is used in exit-path ∞-categories and in definable/o-minimal stratification theory. A precise version of the 'atelier' axioms could inform the axiomatization of tame geometries, e.g. tame/condensed approaches, though the idea itself is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting unpublished piece of the 'atelier' axiomatics, showing Grothendieck treating strata posets functorially via inverse images of closed sets. The underlying mathematics (posets, Alexandrov topology, uniqueness via sobrification) is standard. The stratification-as-poset-map viewpoint was later developed independently, so this is not a genuinely new result.
transcription_corrections: Margin (rotated) reads roughly: 'il suffit par (1.54) que f(F') soit une partie [fermée?] de F pour que f ... soit ...'; the struck words are uncertain.
'Dans le cas général, on demandera encore que l'application (1.54) soit [?] surjective' — the illegible word is likely 'au moins', i.e. 'soit au moins surjective'.
'Mais dans [-tout-] au moins ... dans les cas [-importants-]' — the parenthetical reads '(comme 𝓕 → Fig(𝓛))'.
The last line reads 'on aura (1.54) bijective pour tout F' (with F, not the uncertain '[?] F').
